title: Can You Put Hardwood Floors in a Kitchen, Bathroom or Basement?
meta: Hardwood in a kitchen: yes. Powder room: yes, engineered. Full bath and basement: mostly not. Wills Flooring explains the rules and prices for Sammamish homes.
keywords: hardwood floors in kitchen, can you put hardwood in a bathroom, hardwood flooring in basement, engineered hardwood kitchen Sammamish WA, hardwood floor moisture rooms
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Kitchen: yes, and it is the room we install hardwood in most. Powder room: yes, with engineered planks. Full bathroom: only engineered, only for careful adults. Basement: solid never, engineered only over a slab that tests dry, and vinyl plank is usually the smarter call.
blocks.detail: Wood does not mind humidity; it minds standing water and moisture from below. Each of these rooms has a different amount of both, which is why the answer changes from door to door. Installation labor is $3.25 per sq ft for engineered or solid at Wills Flooring, material quoted separately.

blocks.html: In Sammamish the question almost never arrives as "can I put wood in a bathroom." It arrives as "we want the same floor everywhere." Plateau homes in Klahanie, Trossachs and Sahalee were built with open main floors where the kitchen, dining and family room are one space, and the builder oak stops at a strip of tile in front of the sink. Homeowners want that seam gone, and while they are at it they ask about the powder room and the daylight basement. Here is where we say yes, where we say engineered only, and where we say no.

items.title: Run it continuous, no threshold
items.text: The whole point is one floor from the front door through the kitchen. Solid or engineered both work in a kitchen on a plywood subfloor. We run the planks straight through where the old tile was, after removing the tile and leveling the backer, so nothing tells you where the kitchen starts.

items.title: Site-finish it if you can
items.text: Prefinished planks have a small bevel at every edge, and in a kitchen those bevels collect drips and grit. An unfinished floor installed at $2.75 per sq ft and then sanded and finished with three coats of Bona water-based seals the seams as one surface. It costs more but wipes like a countertop.

items.title: Protect the two leak points
items.text: Every kitchen hardwood failure we have replaced in Sammamish came from a dishwasher or a fridge line, not from cooking. Braided steel supply lines, a drip pan under the dishwasher and a $20 water alarm behind the fridge cost less than one damaged board.

items.title: Pick a forgiving floor
items.text: White oak, hickory or maple in a matte or satin finish hides the drips and crumbs of a family kitchen. Dark stains and glossy sheens show every water spot. Wire-brushed textures forgive dropped pans. We bring samples from Metropolitan Hardwood and set them under the kitchen light.

blocks.text: Basements: the slab decides, not you

items.text: We test slab moisture at the estimate with a calcium chloride kit or an in-slab relative humidity probe. Above the adhesive maker's limit, hardwood is off the table no matter what finish you like.
items.note: Sammamish daylight basements on sloped lots often test dry on the walk-out side and damp at the back wall.

items.text: Solid boards have to be nailed into wood, and the concrete under a basement breathes moisture year round. Solid wood on a slab cups by the first winter.
items.note: This is a manufacturer rule, not a Wills preference.

items.text: On a dry slab we glue engineered planks down with a moisture-cure urethane adhesive that also acts as a vapor retarder. Floating engineered over a pad is the other option, with a 6 mil poly barrier.
items.note: Labor is $3.25 per sq ft either way. Adhesive and prep are quoted at the estimate.

items.d: Or choose vinyl plank and sleep well
items.text: Most Sammamish basements we look at get vinyl plank at $2.50 per sq ft labor, matched in tone to the hardwood upstairs. It shrugs off a seep the hardwood would not.
items.note: A dehumidifier is a good idea with either floor.

blocks.note: Labor only. Material, tile removal, leveling and adhesive are quoted at the free estimate.

blocks.html: A typical plateau main floor with the kitchen included runs about 1,400 sq ft: 1,400 × $3.25 = $4,550 in installation labor, plus the flooring you choose. Adding a 40 sq ft powder room to that run is another 40 × $3.25 = $130, which is why we almost always say yes to the powder room. A 13-stair flight down to a daylight basement is 13 × $125 = $1,625 if you want hardwood treads to match.

blocks.title: The rule we will not bend:
blocks.text: We do not install hardwood over a slab we have not moisture tested, even if another company already said it was fine. The test takes minutes at the free estimate, and it is the difference between a floor that lasts and a floor we replace in two years.
When to stop and choose something else

items.html: Small children and a tub. A bath-time splash every night is standing water every night. Vinyl plank in a matching tone is the honest answer here.
The dog's water bowl lives in the kitchen. Hardwood is still fine, but put the bowl on a tray with a lip. Bowls are the number one source of the black ring we sand out of kitchen floors.
Any history of basement water. If the previous owner mentioned a wet corner, or the lot drains toward the house, the basement gets vinyl plank. We will not be talked into hardwood there.
A cold, unconditioned basement. Big swings in temperature and humidity move wood more than a steady damp does. Condition the space first or pick a floor that does not care.

HOA and resale. Sammamish buyers expect hardwood on the main floor and are indifferent to it in bathrooms. Spend the hardwood budget where it is seen, and see our hardwood installation page for what is included.

faq.q: Is engineered hardwood waterproof enough for a bathroom?
faq.a: No hardwood is waterproof. Engineered planks have a plywood or high-density core that resists swelling from humidity far better than solid boards, so they tolerate a well-ventilated adult bathroom. They still fail from standing water, a leaking toilet seal or a tub that overflows. Treat it as water-tolerant, not waterproof.

faq.q: Can you put solid hardwood in a kitchen?
faq.a: Yes. Solid oak, maple or hickory over a plywood subfloor is a normal kitchen floor and has been for a century. Use a matte or satin finish, protect the dishwasher and fridge lines, and wipe up spills the same day. Kitchens are the room we install hardwood in most often in Sammamish.

faq.q: What is the best way to install hardwood in a basement?
faq.a: Engineered planks glued to a moisture-tested slab with a urethane adhesive that doubles as a vapor retarder. Floating engineered over a poly barrier and pad is the alternative. Solid hardwood cannot be installed below grade. If the slab tests wet, we recommend vinyl plank instead.

faq.q: How much does it cost to add hardwood to a kitchen in Sammamish?
faq.a: Wills Flooring installation labor is $3.25 per sq ft for engineered or solid, with a 500 sq ft minimum. A 250 sq ft kitchen done alone bills at the minimum, so most homeowners do the kitchen as part of the main floor. Tile removal, leveling and the flooring itself are quoted at the free estimate.

faq.q: Will hardwood in a kitchen hurt resale value?
faq.a: The opposite. Sammamish buyers consistently prefer one continuous hardwood floor across the kitchen and living areas over a tile island in the kitchen. Where hardwood does not help resale is in full bathrooms and basements, which buyers expect to be tile or vinyl plank.

faq.q: Can I put hardwood over the existing kitchen tile?
faq.a: Usually not. Tile adds height, hides subfloor problems and gives nails nothing to bite. We remove the tile, repair and level the subfloor and run the new hardwood at the same height as the adjoining rooms. Removal and prep are quoted at the estimate after we look at the tile.
